security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU TCG translates CHERI capability store instructions (SCAP) using the old spec that applies SL permission filtering on loads rather than stores. Specifically, in the capability store fast-path or helper (e.g., cheri_cap_store), the SL bit in acperm is either (a) checked on load instead of store, or (b) not checked at all on store, causing capabilities stored with SL=0 to pass through unfiltered, while loads are incorrectly gated by SL.
security_spec.summary: Inverted SL permission semantics — if SL filtering is applied on capability loads instead of stores, a compromised or buggy compartment could write capabilities that survive a non-filtering store and are later loaded without the intended SL sanitization, violating CHERI memory-safety guarantees.

findings.finding: CHERI capability store instructions (SCAP) and SL permission filtering code do not exist in this upstream QEMU repository. The described vulnerability pattern (cheri_cap_store, acperm, SL_PERM, store_local, cap_store) returned zero matches across all target/riscv/ source files (translate.c, op_helper.c, cpu_bits.h, cpu.h, helper.h, machine.c, and all insn_trans/*.c.inc translation files). No CHERI-dedicated files, branches, or tags exist. This is expected — CHERI support is maintained in separate downstream forks such as CTSRD-CHERI/qemu.
findings.snippet: No CHERI capability store code present in this repository.
